This HEAD-only branch bypasses the `payload.locked` guard in `sendWebStream()`. With a `ReadableStream` locked via `stream.getReader()`, an explicit HEAD handler that calls `reply.send(stream)` now returns HTTP 200 with an empty body while the stream remains locked. `cancel()` rejects, the rejection is only logged, and execution still reaches `safeWriteHead()`/`sendTrailer()`. The normal path instead raises `FST_ERR_REP_READABLE_STREAM_LOCKED`, so this turns an invalid response into an apparent success.

Please apply the same locked-stream validation before cancellation and add an explicit HEAD regression test using a locked Web Stream. I ran the existing related HEAD/trailer tests (34/34 pass), which confirms this case is currently uncovered.

rule: When a new hook, option, or API is added to the runtime, its TypeScript overload in types/*.d.ts must be updated in the same PR; omitting it causes excess-property or compile-time errors for TypeScript consumers.

evidence.quote:
[P1] Keep `url`/`path` as an at-least-one requirement

Making both properties optional here lets TypeScript accept `fastify().route({ method: 'GET', handler })` with neither route location. I reproduced this on head baac6fb5 with TypeScript 6.0.3: the call compiles cleanly, but the same object throws `ERR_ASSERTION: The path could not be empty` at runtime. This is a regression from the previous required `url` contract, and the new positive-only type tests do not catch it. Please model these fields as an at-least-one union, for example `({ url: string; path?: string } | { path: string; url?: string })` intersected with the shared route options, and add a negative type assertion for the neither-present case.

The new test establishes `onSend` as a supported `setNotFoundHandler` option, but the public TypeScript overload in `types/instance.d.ts` accepts only `preValidation` and `preHandler`; TypeScript consumers therefore get an excess-property error for this API. Add the `onSend` callback/async callback types and a corresponding type test (and update the lifecycle documentation that currently says `callNotFound()` only calls the configured `preHandler`).

`onRegister` still falls through to the generic validation below. Its newly valid async signature has three declared parameters, so `addHook('onRegister', async (instance, newInstance, options) => {})`—which the updated type test accepts—now throws `FST_ERR_HOOK_INVALID_ASYNC_HANDLER`. Include `onRegister` in the branch that rejects four-argument async handlers (the extra argument would be `done`) or otherwise special-case its new arity, and add a runtime regression test.

rule: Documentation must not overstate or contradict actual runtime behaviour; when a guard has known exceptions or bypasses, the prose must be scoped accurately and all parameters must be described.

evidence.quote: The signature now lists `instance`, but the explanatory text immediately below still says that `routeOptions` is the sole parameter. Please describe both parameters here to avoid contradictory public API documentation.

This overstates the validation boundary. `ContentType` deliberately ignores malformed parameters (`test/content-type.test.js:162-181`), and bodyless methods bypass this check (`lib/handle-request.js:35-37`), so not every syntactically invalid `Content-Type` yields a 415. Scope the statement to parsed payloads and invalid type/subtype syntax.

This issue also appears on line 65 of the same file.

The statement "The stack trace is never included" is too absolute: if a route-level response schema serializer is present, `fallbackErrorHandler()` passes an object that still exposes `error.stack` via the prototype chain, so a schema that includes `stack` could serialize it. The docs should scope this to Fastify's built-in error serializer (and/or mention that schemas can still include it).

The example comment says 4xx errors are "safe to expose", but `statusCode < 500` doesn't guarantee the message is non-sensitive (it only indicates the HTTP class). Consider softening this wording so it doesn't imply blanket safety.

rule: Doc examples that delete symbol-keyed properties must use Object.getOwnPropertySymbols() or Reflect.ownKeys(); Object.keys() never returns symbol keys and silently skips the intended operation.

In the `buildPrettyMeta` example, `Object.keys(cleanMeta)` will never return symbol keys, so the `typeof k === 'symbol'` check never matches and the example does not actually remove symbol properties as the comment suggests.
